judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The image is the photo of candidate Lula in the election results widget, with alt="Lula". That alt names the person shown, which is the right text alternative for a candidate photo. It is not a file name or a placeholder, even though the file is Lula.png. The "16%" in the crop is the end of the separate "45,16%" vote-bar text overlapping the photo, not part of the image. So the suggested alt "Lula com um selo de 16%" would be wrong.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the Google Ad Manager banner (an Ágora/Bradesco ad). Its img is the only content of a link to the advertiser, with alt="Advertisement". The image is mostly text ("A evolução do seu jeito de investir", "Descubra uma nova experiência com o app Ágora", "Saiba mais"). "Advertisement" gives neither that text nor the link's purpose, so the functional image has no equivalent text alternative. That is a real 1.1.1 failure on the page (the ad is third-party and rotates, but it is part of the page as served). The link also fails 2.4.4.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the WhatsApp channel link in the newsletter box: the WhatsApp brand logo (white glyph on WhatsApp green #22d467, on a #fbfbfb box). The 1.97:1 measurement is right, but the Understanding document for 1.4.11 exempts logos under the essential exception and says the exemption carries over to a UI component that is a logo. The logo is shown in its brand colours. Next to it is an "INSCREVA-SE" text link to the same WhatsApp URL. So this is not a 1.4.11 failure; at most it is the best-practice note in the Understanding document.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the video.js player in the home page grid. Its container is explicitly marked lang="pt-br" (role=region), yet its accessible text is English: the region label "Video Player", the "Play Video" button, the ad video's title "Advertisement", and control texts such as "Mute", "Current Time" and "Seek to live". These are English phrases, not proper names or vernacular, and they are programmatically marked Portuguese. A pt-BR screen reader voice will mispronounce them, so 3.1.2 fails as claimed. The patch is poor, though. Setting lang="en" on the whole player is not the right fix; the player's strings should be localized to pt-BR, or each English string marked lang="en".

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the Google Programmable Search box inside the site's slide-out menu. At capture time the menu was closed (the field was off-screen at y=-1077), and the snapshot marks the adjacent search button, an SVG titled "pesquisar", as hidden. When the menu is open, the screenshot shows the field with a magnifying-glass icon beside it. The Understanding document for 3.3.2 names exactly this case: a global search field paired with a loupe icon has that icon as its visible label. So the field has a visible cue. The low contrast of that icon would be a 1.4.11 question, not a 3.3.2 failure.
